stories.title: 12-week RCT: 40C hot-water immersion improves brachial artery function like aerobic exercise - but exercise also wins on femoral arteries
stories.summary: foundmyfitness recaps a randomized controlled trial (Costa et al., Experimental Physiology, doi 10.1113/EP094115): 31 inactive older adults (58 +/- 7 years, BMI ~30) were randomized to 12 weeks of 3x40-min moderate aerobic exercise, 3x40-min 40C hot-water immersion, or inactive control; brachial-artery flow-mediated dilation improved with both exercise and hot water, but femoral-artery FMD improved with exercise only, and neither intervention moved resting blood pressure or pulse-wave velocity. For builders on heat-therapy and vascular-aging interventions this is the cleanest head-to-head human RCT of heat vs exercise to date, with the practical finding that heat is a partial substitute for exercise, not a full one. Caveat: it is one small (n=31) randomized trial in community-dwelling overweight older adults - the paper was published 19 Jul 2026 (the in-window item is the expert recap, 21 Sep), fitness was not re-tested post-intervention, and no dose-response was established.

corroboration.name: Costa et al. 2026, Exp Physiol (full text on PMC)
